description:
## At-Tur - The Mountain

**(Revealed at Mecca)**

**49 Verses in 2 Sections**

## Sections Of Surah At-Tur

1. The Day Of Judgment Described.

2. A Challenge To Bring Something Similar To Qur'an.

## Important Topics

1. The assurance of the coming of the Calamity which none shall avert (Verses 1-8)

2. The disbelievers will be shown the torments which they denied (Verses 13-15)

3. The blissful enjoyments that await the pious ones (Verses 17-20)

4. The ordinance regarding the Night Prayer (Tahajjud) (Verse 49)

## At-Tur Section 1: The Day Of Judgment Described

- The Coming Of The Day Of Judgment Is Certain
- The Blissful Recompense Awaiting The Believers And The Woeful Torment Which The Disbelievers Shall Have

In the name of God, the Beneficent the Merciful

## At-Tur Section 2: A Challenge To Bring Something Similar To Qur'an

- The Respite Allowed To The Disbelievers
- A Challenge To Those Who Disbelieve In The Qur'an, To Bring At Least Something Similar To It
- The Disbelievers Shall Be Punished In This World And In The Hereafter
- To Glorify God At Night And At Dawn

4.1: Concerning the expansion of the realm of creation, refer to Verse <{["Q", "51:47"]}>.

translations.1: By (I swear.) the Mountain 'Tur' (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "95:2"]}>.)
translations.4: And by the House (The Ka'bah.) populated (Visited by frequent worshippers.)
translations.5: And by the Roof (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "16:26"]}>; <{["Q", "21:32"]}>.) elevated (Something beyond the physical expanse.)
translations.6: And by the Sea (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "40:72"]}>; <{["Q", "81:6"]}>.) boiling
translations.7: Verily the chastisement of thy Lord shall indeed come to pass
translations.8: There is none to repel (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "70:2"]}>.) it
translations.9: On the Day (The happenings on the eve of the Resurrection for the Final Judgment.) when the heaven shall reel a (Terrible) reeling (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "82:1"]}>; <{["Q", "84:1"]}>.)
translations.10: And the mountains shall fly an (awful) flight (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "81:3"]}>; <{["Q", "77:10"]}>; <{["Q", "78:20"]}>.)
translations.11: Woe then that day unto those who belie the Truth (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "70:6"]}>-<{["Q", "70:10"]}>; <{["Q", "83:10"]}>.)
translations.12: Those who, in vain sport (In discourse.) do play
translations.13: The Day on which they shall be driven unto the hell-fire with a violent drive
translations.14: [And it shall be said unto them]: 'This is the Fire (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "36:63"]}>.) which ye used to belie'
translations.15: What! Is it sorcery then? Or ye see it not?
translations.16: Enter ye into it then be ye patient, or be ye not patient, alike shall it be unto you; certainly, shall ye be recompensed what ye used to do
translations.17: Verily the pious ones shall be in the gardens (Of Paradise.) amidst the bounties (therein)
translations.18: Rejoicing in what gave them their Lord, and saved them their Lord from the chastisement of the Hell
translations.19: (It will be said unto them)'. "Eat ye and drink ye in health and delight for what ye used to do'"
translations.20: Reclining on thrones ranged; And We will unite (Make their offsprings follow them in their goodness thus multiply or add the reward of one with that of the other, for both of them.) them with Huries (maidens pure) with large (lovely) eyes (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "37:48"]}>-<{["Q", "37:49"]}>; <{["Q", "44:54"]}>; <{["Q", "55:56"]}>; <{["Q", "55:72"]}> <{["Q", "56:22"]}>; <{["Q", "56:35"]}>-<{["Q", "56:37"]}>.)
translations.21: And those who believe and follow them their offspring in faith, We will unite (Make their offsprings follow them in their goodness thus multiply or add the reward of one with that of the other, for both of them.) with them their offspring and We will lessen not unto them aught of their (good) deeds; Every man shall for what he hath wrought, be responsible (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "53:39"]}>; <{["Q", "74:38"]}>.)
translations.22: And We will provide with fruits and flesh of what they desire (What they would be pleased to have. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "56:20"]}>; <{["Q", "56:21"]}>.)
translations.23: They shall pass therein to one another a cup (Of drink which would not corrupt the mind or affect the health) wherein shall not be any vanity nor a sin (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "56:25"]}>.)
translations.24: And there shall go around them (serving them) youths (handsome) as if they are imbedded pearls (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "56:17"]}>; <{["Q", "76:19"]}>.)
translations.25: And some shall accost the others making mutual enquiries
translations.26: They will say: 'Verily we feared ere (this) in regard to our families'
translations.27: But God hath bestowed His grace on us, and He hath saved us from the chastisement of the scorching wind
translations.28: Verily, we used ere this to call upon Him; Verily, He is the Benign, the Most Merciful
translations.29: So thou remind on (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) for thou, by the grace (Bounty.) of thy Lord (on thee), art neither a soothsayer, nor a mad man
translations.30: Or say they (about thee O' Our Apostle!) 'A poet (is he)! Let us wait (What the people said.) for him (The Holy Prophet.) some fatal adversity (Death.) (drawn) by time!'
translations.31: Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!). "Wait ye, and verily I too with you am of those who wait' (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "9:15"]}> and <{["Q", "9:52"]}>.)"
translations.32: Or is it that bid them their deliberations, to do this, or are they an inordinate (Rebels.) people?
translations.33: Or say they (that): 'He (The Holy Prophet.) hath forged it (the Qur'an)? Nay! they believe not (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "69:41"]}>-<{["Q", "69:47"]}>.) '
translations.34: Let them then bring a dis-course like unto it, if they be truthful (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "2:23"]}>; <{["Q", "10:38"]}>; <{["Q", "11:13"]}>.)
translations.35: Or were they created by nothing? Or are they themselves the creators? (See note on the Existence of God in the introduction.)
translations.36: Or created they the heavens and the earth? Nay! they have no certainty (Firmness of belief.)
translations.37: Or with them are the treasures of thy Lord, Or hold they the absolute authority?
translations.38: Or for them is a ladder by which they can (climb up into the heaven and) listen (to the angels)? Then let the listener of theirs bring a proof manifest
translations.39: Or for Him are daughters and for ye sons? (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "16:57"]}>; <{["Q", "43:16"]}>.)
translations.40: Or thou asketh of them any recompense, that they are burdened with the weight of debt? (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "68:46"]}>.)
translations.41: Or with them is the unseen that they write it down? (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "68:47"]}>.)
translations.42: Or intend they to lay (Scheming.) snares for thee? But those who disbelieve are themselves the snared ones
translations.43: Or for them is a god other than God? Hallowed is God from what they associate (Creating equals to Him - False Gods - Worshipping angels as the daughters and Jesus as the Son of God.) (with Him)
translations.44: And if they see a portion of the heaven coming down, they would say: '(they are) clouds piled up (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "26:187"]}>.) '
translations.45: Leave them then until they encounter the Day of theirs where-in they shall be smitten (With Thunderbolt.) (with terror) to swoon (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "39:68"]}>.)
translations.46: A day wherein their devices shall avail them not aught, nor shall they be helped
translations.47: And verily for those who did injustice there shall be a chastisement besides that, but most of them know it not
translations.48: And wait thou patiently for the command of thy Lord, for verily thou art before Our (Purview.) eyes, and celebrate thou the praise of thy Lord when thou risest (Thus, every act of the Holy Prophet will be the view of the Lord. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "50:39"]}>-<{["Q", "50:40"]}>.)
translations.49: And in the night too, celebrate thou His Glory and at the setting of the stars

exegesis.1:
The adjuration is by five things to assert the certainty of future events in the most emphatic terms in verse 7 to 28 - the coming of judgement and the passing away of this phenomenal world; the future ill consequences of ill deeds; and the future attainment of bliss and complete realisation of Allah's grace and mercy as recompense for good deeds.

Tur, i.e., The Mount, The Mount Sinai, which stands for all that happened in the ministry of Moses. There is a mention of it in <{["Q", "95:2"]}>.
exegesis.2:
The Book inscribed 'The Secured Tablet' called the Lawh al-Mahfooz., Some commentators mean the Holy Qur'an and some others mean Torah which was given to Moses on the Mount Sinai, inscribed on Tablets of Stone.

With the exception Tur which clearly refers to Mount Sinai- The rest of the references are to things not terrestrial. The written Book in the lustrous sheet, refers neither to Torah nor to Qur'an nor either to other Scripture in its revealed form. Therefore, the Book will refer to whatever is inscribed on 'Lawh al-Mahfooz', on the Secured Tablet (A.P.).
exegesis.3: The Scroll unfolded is The Holy Qur'an, which is unfolded by a revelation for the benefit of mankind as a whole and for all times.
exegesis.4:
Bayt al-Ma'mur (the much-frequented house), the Holy Ka'ba, which is always full of the visitors, the pilgrims, on all days of the year, the Ka'ba which was cleared of the idols in it by the Holy Prophet (S) and Imam ''Ali ('a) and re-dedicated to the worship of the One True God.

Some commentators say that by the word 'Bayt', i.e., house, it means the 'Bayt al-Ma'mur' a place of adoration for the heavenly bodies.

So, 'Bayt al-Ma'mur' does not refer to any terrestrial sacred place of worship none of which is ever filled with worshippers all the days of the year; but it refers to the heavenly place of worship as narrated by ''Ali Ibn Abi Talib ('a): "The heavenly place of worship which is visited every day by a multitude of angels who never revisit it again", which implies the ever increase of the angels which means the ever expansion of the realm of creation<{["F", 1]}> (A.P.).
exegesis.5: "The roof elevated" is the canopy of heaven, to whose height or sublimity no limit can be assigned by the mind of man. The nebular ocean refers to the beyond physical expanse. Except Tur, all above-noted signs or things are celestial.
exegesis.6: The Nebular Oceans within the heart of the earth, within the suns - and the other heavenly bodies (A.P.).
exegesis.7: Verses 7 to 10 illustrate with the solemnity the reference to the above great things of wonder which are facts, the coming Doom from God also, is assured as a reality which shall come to pass.
exegesis.11: The day of reckoning will be a day of woe to the unjust who belied the signs of Allah, just as it will be a day of joy and bliss to the righteous believers. Every evil thought or deed has its own retributive and punishable chain of consequences. Whatever is done in this life is a preparation for the hereafter, which the disbelievers will find a reality after the day of judgement, not a farce. They did not take notice of the signs of Allah nor paid attention to the warnings the messengers of Allah gave them, so there will be no time for repentance. They will roast in hell, whether they endure it or not.
exegesis.12: The reference is to those who ridicule the warnings about the day of requital, and spend their time in sport and vain amusements, the time which everyone has to avail of, to prepare for himself for the life hereafter specially to give the account of his life, to the Lord.
exegesis.15: The disbelievers would then be asked, if they now realise that the warnings that the apostles of God, gave them about the Day of Judgment, were not fake or false but truth which they see with their own eyes.
exegesis.16:
In the worldly punishment one is punished for an act but in the natural punishment one receives, which one does here, i.e., the final shape of what the actions assume (A.P.).

The righteous believers will be in the land of eternal bliss. By their own effort and striving they won Allah's grace and mercy.
exegesis.17:
Everyone, as an individual, will have full satisfaction (in whatever he or she does) dignity and joy of companionship. Every one will be purified but will not be merged into one sameness.

There will be a general social satisfaction shared with all whom they loved in this earthly life, all near and dear ones, provided they had believed and done good deeds, because each individual is responsible for his conduct and none shall bear another's burden, as stressed in <{["Q", "2:48"]}>, <{["Q", "2:123"]}>, <{["Q", "2:254"]}>; <{["Q", "6:164"]}>; <{["Q", "17:15"]}>; <{["Q", "35:18"]}>; <{["Q", "39:7"]}> and <{["Q", "53:38"]}>.

Relationship of this life has no value in the hereafter unless it is sanctioned by the ties of true faith.
exegesis.20: Though the Hoor or the Ghilman, would not be the beings, same as the imperfect, impure and the mortal human beings of this life, they are beings, purity and beauty embodied who could not be aptly explained with comparison to anything in this world which could not be compared to that of the hereafter. Make their offspring follow them in their goodness<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.21:
Note the doctrine of the personal responsibility of every individual man or woman – None shall bear the burden of the other - This aspect of the individual responsibility, the realization of which is essential to make man live a strictly controlled and perfectly cautious life, is repeatedly stressed as in <{["Q", "2:48"]}>, <{["Q", "2:123"]}>, <{["Q", "2:254"]}>; <{["Q", "6:164"]}>; <{["Q", "17:15"]}>; <{["Q", "35:18"]}>; <{["Q", "39:7"]}> and <{["Q", "53:38"]}>.

Clearly asserts that mere relationship in this life is of no value in the hereafter unless it is confirmed with the ties of faith. (A.P.)
exegesis.34: Of all the religious scriptures of the world which claim to be heavenly or sacred in any other way, the Holy Qur'an is the only Scripture which has repeatedly challenged its disbelievers to bring a part of its kind and about 1400 years have elapsed and yet none could reply to it. This is one of the living miracles of the Holy Qur'an that its text is inimitable, even from the literary aspect of its beauty and superiority and none could corrupt it nor effect any change in its arrangement<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.35:
The disbelievers are asked that if they believed, that they had been created without a Creator or without any purpose.

This lays the fundamental axiom which is one of the and scientific propositions are based - that an effect of a phenomenon or by itself (A.P.).
exegesis.38:
Or is it that they have any ladder to get into basic foundations on which all philosophic cannot come into being out of nothing heaven to know the secrets<{["F", 1]}>.

This applies to those who claim that besides the logical method of the approach to the moral, social and theological problems, they have special ways of direct communion or direct touch with the divine sources. Claims of such nature have no value unless it is supported by clear and irrefutable evidence, such as miracles (A.P.).
exegesis.49: About spending a part of the night in prayer, see Verses <{["Q", "17:78"]}>-<{["Q", "17:79"]}>. And at the setting of the stars, see Verse <{["Q", "113:1"]}>.
